videos.script: Until now every image came from somebody else. This lesson builds one, for Ana's own service. {{file}} Six lines are enough: a base image, a folder, a copy, a compile, a port and a command. {{build}} The build prints one numbered step for each piece of work, and the program answers on her machine. {{signals}} Then one line changes, and stopping the container takes ten seconds instead of a fifth of one. The difference is whether a shell sits between Docker and the program. {{args}} Then build arguments and environment variables: one lives during the build, the other in every container. {{context}} And last, the context. Docker sends the whole folder to the builder, and a password file ends up inside the image. One small file keeps it out.
